### Animations of animal movements with R

If you have any issues with this code after the workshop, please reach out and I'm happy to help. My email is wgreentree\@outlook.com

For additional details/resources glatos: <https://rdrr.io/github/jsta/glatos/man/glatos.html> <https://github.com/ocean-tracking-network/glatos>

Examples of extra things to try with gganimate (e.g., shadow wakes instead of paths behind points; fish image instead of point using ggimage package - this works really well): <https://goodekat.github.io/presentations/2019-isugg-gganimate-spooky/slides.html#1>

More information for making maps with R, with lots of example code: <https://github.com/wesleygreentree/CSEE2024-R-maps>

```{r Install packages}
## install packages that you don't already have:
install.packages(c("remotes", "sf", "stars", "tidyverse", "basemaps", "gganimate",
                   "terra", "tidyterra",  "ggnewscale", "geosphere"))
install.packages("rnaturalearthhires",
  repos = "https://ropensci.r-universe.dev",
  type = "source") # high resolution basemaps for RNaturalEarth
install.packages("rnaturalearth")
remotes::install_github("ocean-tracking-network/glatos") # works best if installed from OTN GitHub

# load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(glatos) 
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(basemaps)
library(geosphere)
library(stars)
library(gganimate)
library(ggnewscale)
```

#### 1. View detection data

First, let's take make a simple map to show each fish's detections.

A problem immediately jumps out: The movement tracks cross land.

```{r Static map to view detection data}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = nova.scotia) +
  geom_path(data = salmon.dets,
             aes(x = decimalLongitude, y = decimalLatitude, colour = tagName),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-67.2, -66.8), ylim = c(44.85, 45.2),
           expand = FALSE) +
  theme_bw()
# Wes - remember to include receiver stations
```

#### 2. Constrain movement tracks to stay in water

We need to constrain the movement tracks to stay in the water.

We will need a shapefile of the ocean. When animating the movements of coastal species in regions with complex coastlines, we need a very high resolution shapefile to ensure that movement tracks do not cross small islands or other coastal land masses.

-   A very high resolution shapefile of Canada's oceans is available at <https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/6c78fb2f-d23b-45b4-b3af-cc6f6cc4fff8>

-   A medium resolution shapefile of the world's oceans is available at <https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/10m-physical-vectors/10m-ocean/>

If we only have access to a shapefile of land masses (e.g., `bc.coast`), we can convert that shapefile to an ocean shapefile, as follows:

```{r Make ocean shapefile}
# extract the coordinates of the area of the shapefile

# WES
# WES - maybe instead use the study area for faster computation
# WES

box <- data.frame(t(data.frame(st_bbox(nova.scotia))))
nova.scotia.poly <- st_sfc(st_polygon(list(cbind(
  c(box$xmin, box$xmax, box$xmax, box$xmin, box$xmin),
  c(box$ymin, box$ymin, box$ymax, box$ymax, box$ymin)))),
  crs = 4326)

# The sf package uses spherical geometry, but many of the shapefiles that we encounter in the real world (including bc.coast) were developed with planar geometry. Therefore, we will tell sf to use planar geometry.
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE) 

# make an ocean shape file by inverting bc.coast
ocean <- st_difference(nova.scotia.poly, st_union(st_combine(nova.scotia)))

# view bc.ocean shapefile
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ocean, fill = "lightblue")
```

Next, we will use `bc.ocean` to make a **transition layer**. A transition layer is a raster that defines where a tagged animal's movement track can (water) and cannot go (land). In other words, the transition layer is a grid of 1's and 0's that dictate where a movement track can and cannot go.

We produce the transition layer with `glatos::make_transition()`. Since the transition layer is converting ocean polygons (called "vector data") to a grid (called "raster data"), we manually set the desired resolution of those grid cells.

```{r Make transition layer}
# to speed up computation, we will limit bc.ocean to the area needed

range(dets$longitude)
range(dets$latitude)

study.area.box <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -126, ymin = 49.4, xmax = -123, ymax = 49.), 
                          crs = st_crs(4326))

study.area.ocean <- st_crop(bc.ocean, study.area.box)

bc.ocean <- sf::as_Spatial(bc.ocean) # glatos requires that the ocean layer be a SpatialPolygons
class(bc.ocean)

# Make translation layer.
Sys.time()
ocean.trans <- glatos::make_transition(bc.ocean, res = c(0.1, 0.1),
                                epsg = 4326) # 0.002 decimal degrees
Sys.time()
plot(ocean.trans)
#saveRDS(ocean.trans) # really useful to save this as an RDS object. For the larger study areas that we typically work in, it can take very long to create. The transition layer I use for the BC coast is 35 MB

# visualize raster resolution
bc.coast <- vect(bc.coast)
dim(bc.coast)
bc.rast <- rasterize(bc.coast)

ocean.trans.terra <- terra::rast(ocean.trans$rast) 

ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = ocean.trans.terra) +
  geom_point(data = tags, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude), colour = "yellow")

ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = ocean.trans.terra) +
  geom_point(data = tags, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude), colour = "yellow") + 
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE, xlim = c(-124.75, -124.6), ylim = c(49.45, 49.55))
```

```{r Interpolate tracks to stay in water}
# detection data in glatos format
tags.glatos <- dplyr::select(tags, tagname, datetimeUTC, longitude, latitude)
names(tags.glatos) <- c("animal_id", "detection_timestamp_utc", "deploy_long", "deploy_lat")

tracks <- glatos::interpolate_path(tags.glatos, 
                           trans = ocean.trans$transition, 
                           lnl_thresh = 2, int_time_stamp = 1800)
# interpolates a position every hour. Can increase to every 6 hours, day etc... but larger time gaps between interpolation points increases the chance that an interpolated point is on land
# takes a long time for 50-100 tags with 100,000s of detections. I run on the lab's 32 GB RAM desktop, can take 2 hours (may run faster in parallel). In some cases, will not run on my personal laptop (16 GB RAM).
# can run in batches, e.g. only 10 tags at a time, if this is an issue

# view interpolated paths
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ocean, fill = "lightblue") + 
  geom_path(data = tracks, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = animal_id)) +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE)
```

```{r Animation}
# load in satellite basemap with the basemaps package
satellite.box <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -125.4, ymin = 49.2, xmax = -124.1, ymax = 49.95),
                  crs = st_crs(4326))
satellite <- basemaps::basemap_stars(ext = satellite.box, map_service = "esri",
                                     map_type = "world_imagery", map_res = 1)
class(satellite) # stars: raster cubes (multiple raster layers)
sf::st_crs(satellite) # 3857 (Web Mercator)
satellite.rgb <- stars::st_rgb(satellite) # converts 3 satellite layers (RGB) to color

# convert tracks from WGS 1984 to Web Mercator (CRS 3857)
tracks <- sf::st_as_sf(tracks, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = st_crs(4326))
tracks <- sf::st_transform(tracks, crs = st_crs(3857))
coords <- do.call(rbind, sf::st_geometry(tracks)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% setNames(c("longitude","latitude")) # warning isn't an issue
tracks <- cbind(tracks[1:3], coords)

# make point disappear at the final detection, so it doesn't stay in the animation
tag.ids <- sort(unique(tracks$animal_id))
tracks$eventID <- seq(1, nrow(tracks))

last.det <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = 0, ncol = 4))
names(last.det) <- c("animal_id", "bin_timestamp", "record_type", "eventID")
for (i in 1:length(tag.ids)) {
  tag.sub <- subset(tracks, animal_id == tag.ids[i])
  sub.last <- tail(tag.sub, 1)
  out <- select(sub.last, animal_id, bin_timestamp, record_type, eventID)
  last.det <- rbind(last.det, out)
}

tracks$last_det <- FALSE
tracks$last_det[tracks$eventID %in% last.det$eventID] <- TRUE
tracks$tag_det <- paste(tracks$animal_id, tracks$last_det)

# example receiver locations: for actual study, use all the receivers not just those detecting tags of course
dets <- subset(tracks, record_type == "detection")
unique.det.locations <- dets %>% group_by(longitude, latitude) %>% tally() 

# make animation
animation <- ggplot() +
  #satellite map
  geom_stars(data = satellite.rgb) +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  
  # receiver locations
  geom_point(data = unique.det.locations,
             aes(x = longitude, y = latitude), colour = "#F3E356") +
  
  # tag tracks
  geom_path(data = tracks,
            aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                group = animal_id, color = animal_id),
            alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#5BBAF2", "#e3766e")) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
  geom_point(data = tracks, 
            aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                group = animal_id, color = tag_det),
            size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#5BBAF2", "transparent", "#e3766e", "transparent")) +
  
  # animate
  gganimate::transition_reveal(bin_timestamp) +
  labs(title = "DateTime: {lubridate::as_date(frame_along)}") +
  gganimate::ease_aes("linear") +
  
  # theme
  theme_void() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
        plot.title = element_text(color = "white"))

gganimate::anim_save("animations/example-animation.gif",
          animation = animation,
          width = 12, height = 12, units = "cm", res = 600, nframes = 200,
          bg = "transparent") # this did work actually!
# to initially check that the animation code works, I run with res = 100, nframes = 50 and then increase to res = 600, nframes = 200 (20 second video with 600 dpi)
# can take an hour or more to save large animations

# note that the pink tag was only detected at the northwest receiver for the last few months, so the point remains present much longer than the blue point at its last location

```
